# Continuous integration

`workflows/ci.yml` runs on pull requests, default-branch pushes, and manual dispatches. Every check is its own job and the jobs run in parallel, so a run takes as long as its slowest check. A newer push to the same branch or pull request cancels the run in progress. All CI helpers run with Bun, pinned by `.bun-version`, including in Swift scaffolds.

Actions are pinned to commit SHAs. Dependabot checks for action updates weekly.

Bun jobs run the root `lint:ci`, `typecheck`, and `test` scripts, one job each. This repo has no JavaScript `build` script. Each takes seconds, so they start at once and run on every change, with no change detection in front of them. Keep CI checks read-only. `test` passes until tests are added. `.bun-version` and `packageManager` pin Bun to the version used during scaffolding; update them together. Commit `bun.lock` after changing dependencies. CI caches package downloads, then always installs with `--frozen-lockfile`.

The pre-commit hook already ran lint, typecheck, and the tests before the commit existed. CI repeats them for what a hook can't see: a merge, a machine without the hooks, and the build. A CI failure the hook could have caught is a hook bug, so fix the hook. Tests follow the `tests` skill: logic only, in-process, never in a browser or a simulator. A new check is a package script first. Add it to the hook if it finishes in seconds, and to the `task` matrix as its own job.

Apps using env-manager never install or run it in CI: it is a global tool on the developer's machine. The committed readers (`env.ts`) and, for an Xcode target, `Config/check-env.sh` validate the environment wherever the code runs. Bun loads the tracked `.env` defaults for scripts run from the repository root. Where targets live in subdirectories, the workflow's top-level `env:` repeats the required defaults, because subdirectory scripts and xcodebuild read the process environment, and `Config/Base.xcconfig` includes the generated xcconfig only when it exists. Push deploy credentials to the repository's secrets with `env-manager sync github <env> --only <NAMES>`. Keep defaults harmless and complete enough for CI. If a test needs a credential, supply it explicitly through GitHub Actions secrets. Never commit `.env.local` or native local secrets, and never cache environment outputs.

Swift jobs never boot a simulator. `package` runs `swift test` on the Mac, which compiles every target of the package for macOS and runs the `Core` tests; until a test target exists it runs `swift build`. `app` builds the `PrivateMaps` Xcode scheme in `app-ios` for a generic iOS simulator without signing. Both wait for the `changes` job, which reads the diff so that they take a macOS runner only when native inputs changed. Otherwise each reports success from a Linux runner, which keeps a required check green. Manual dispatches and initial pushes run them, and so do workflow changes. Documentation changes don't. Edit `scripts/changes.ts` when the layout changes. A failure in change detection fails the Swift jobs too. Native jobs run on GitHub's `xcode-27` image (preview; the `macos-*` images still default to older Xcode) with its installed Xcode and Swift, and cache only package dependencies with a key including both toolchain versions. Commit `Package.resolved` when adding dependencies.

Configure branch protection to require the generated job names you need. After renaming the default branch, update the workflow's push branch.
